title: What is known about 1RB0RF_1RC0RD_1LD1LB_1RE0LC_1RA1RD_1RD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_1RC0RD_1LD1LB_1RE0LC_1RA1RD_1RD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine is a bouncer over a periodic background that carries a growing number of defects; the sweeps over the background are proved in Lean for every length, but the defects move and interact in a way no closed description has been found for. No run has come near a halt: the halting state F is entered tens of millions of times per 109 steps and reads 0 every time; no halt in 1010 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The sweep rules
claims.text: 5 rules for all values of the repeat counts and every tape around them: the rightward sweep turns (001001)^n into (110111)^n (D, 6 steps a word), the leftward sweep turns (111011)^n back into (001001)^n (C, 12 steps a word), and the turns at the two ends.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 80,236 cells have been visited and 27,035 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun 1RB0RF_1RC0RD_1LD1LB_1RE0LC_1RA1RD_1RD--- 10000000000 runs 1010 steps without a halt (195,830 ones at the end).

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.507). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.527).

claims.title: Background and defects
claims.text: At the first new cell of every visit to the left end, in the first 108 steps, the tape is a run of 001 words broken by isolated defects: a gap of length 1 (01, call it a) or 4 (00001, b) between consecutive 1s instead of 2. No other gap length occurs away from the two ends. The number of defects grows about linearly with the number of sweeps (about 20 after 50 visits to the left end, 130 after 500, 320 after 1,050).

claims.title: How the defects move
claims.text: Measured in background periods (3 cells) per round trip, the defects drift at one of two speeds, and a whole frozen block of b defects moves rigidly; a defects turn into b at a front that moves one defect per round trip; a lone a runs to the left end, where it is absorbed and the next defect changes kind. The ends create new defects: a sweep over pure background does not reproduce pure background at the ends.

claims.title: Right-end episodes
claims.text: A visit usually adds 3 cells at the left end and 5 at the right; now and then the head stays near the right end for a long time and adds many cells there (11, 17, 27, ... and once 1,725 cells in one visit, near step 2.9·10<sup>7</sup>).

claims.title: The halting state is never close
claims.text: F1 is the only halting transition and F is entered only by A1 (0RF), so a halt needs A on a 1 with another 1 right after it. In the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps F is entered 53,330,403 times and reads 0 every time.

claims.title: The same table as 1RB0RC_1LC1LA, a different start
claims.text: Renaming the states A, B, C, D, E, F of this machine to E, A, B, C, D, F gives the transition table of 1RB0RC_1LC1LA_1RD0LB_1RE1RC_1RA0RF_1RC--- exactly (read off the two tables in their lean/Machine.lean, and checked by a script; there is no Lean theorem for it here). So this machine started on blank tape runs like that one started in state E instead of A. The shared table does not make the halting questions the same. The two machines start from different configurations, and their runs from blank tape never reach a common configuration (checked for the first 200,000 steps, up to the renaming). So one could halt and the other not; each is its own open question. What the two do share is every rule about the table: the sweeps, the background and the way defects move.
claims.where: the transition tables; py/compare_starts.py in the folder of 1RB0RC_1LC1LA

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A proof would have to control the defects: their kinds, speeds and what happens when they meet each other or an end. No closed language of the simple kinds found by the generic searches (windows of up to 11 cells, with run-length parity) contains the run.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The head sweeps from end to end of a tape that is almost all one repeating pattern, carrying a growing crowd of small defects that drift, change kind and are born at the ends. This page shows the pattern, the proved sweep rules, and why a halt would need something no run has shown.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
The sweep rules of lean/Rules.lean, for every repeat count.

sections.heading: A periodic background with drifting defects
sections.html:
The head runs back and forth over the whole tape. A visit to the left end usually adds 3 new cells there and a visit to the right end 5; so the tape grows by about 8 cells per round trip and a round trip costs about as many steps as the tape is wide: hence the square-root growth on both sides.

The tape has two forms. Just after a leftward sweep it is almost entirely the word 001 repeated; just after a rightward sweep almost entirely 111110. Each sweep translates one form into the other, word by word: the rightward sweep in state D turns 001001 into 110111, the leftward one in state C turns 111011 back into 001001 (the same 6-cell period read with another phase). Lean proves both for every length.

What is not background are defects: in the 001 form, gaps between two 1s of length 1 (01, call it a) or 4 (00001, b) instead of 2. They are sparse (a few hundred on tens of thousands of cells), they drift across the tape at a few fixed speeds measured in background periods per round trip, a block of bs moves as a rigid body, as turn into bs at a front that advances one defect per round trip, and a lone a that reaches the left end is absorbed there. The two ends keep creating new defects: a sweep over pure background does not give back pure background at the ends (the end rules below leave 0 001 001 and 0 0001 001).

Every so often the head lingers at the right end and grows it by hundreds of cells in one visit (once 1,725), then the sweeps resume.

sections.heading: The sweep rules
sections.html:
Each row is a theorem of lean/Rules.lean, for every value of n and every tape L, R around it (S> is the head in state S on the next cell, (w)^n n copies of w, 0^inf blank tape). The step counts are exact.

rulefromtostepswhat it says
right_sweepL D> (001001)^n RL (110111)^n D> R6 · nRightward sweep over the background: D turns each 001001 into 110111 (6 steps a word).
left_sweepL (111011)^n C> 0 RL C> 0 (001001)^n R12 · nLeftward sweep over the background: C, with a 0 under the head, turns each 111011 back into 001001 (12 steps a word).
right_endL 0 D> 0^infL C> 0 0 1 0 0 1 0^inf11Right end, arrival in D: five new cells, then C turns back leaving 0 001 001.
right_end_FL 0 F> 0^infL C> 0 0 0 1 0 0 1 0^inf17Right end, arrival in F: the same with one more new cell.
left_end0^inf C> 0 0 1 R0^inf 1 1 1 1 D> R5Left end: C meets the first 001, writes 1111 and turns right in D.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
sections.html:
The only halting transition is F on a 1, and F is entered only from A on a 1 (writing 0, moving right). So the machine halts exactly when A reads a 1 whose right neighbour is also 1. In the rightward sweep over the background, A reads the 1 of a 001 and F then reads the first 0 of the next 001; a halt needs a gap of length 0 (two adjacent 1s) where a 001 should start, at that phase. Gaps of length 0 have never been seen.

In the first 109 steps F is entered 53,330,403 times; it read 0 every time. No halt in 1010 steps.

This machine has the transition table of 1RB0RC_1LC1LA_1RD0LB_1RE1RC_1RA0RF_1RC--- with the states renamed (A, B, C, D, E, F here are E, A, B, C, D, F there). On blank tape it runs like that machine started in state E instead of A. The shared table does not make the halting questions the same. The two machines start from different configurations, and their runs from blank tape never reach a common configuration (checked for the first 200,000 steps, up to the renaming). So one could halt and the other not; each is its own open question. Their runs do show the same background, defects and growth, because every rule about the table holds for both.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.507). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.527).
After 109 steps the tape spans 80,236 cells (7,723 left of the start, 48,627 right), with a density of 1s of 0.337.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Has the transition table of 1RB0RC_1LC1LA with the states renamed, but starts differently, so it is a separate halting question: a bouncer over a periodic background (001 / 111110) carrying sparse drifting defects; no halt in any run.
